name: mummer
why: Genome alignment suite using suffix trees, real bioinformatics you can run on sequences at home.

brief.what_it_is: MUMmer is a command-line suite for aligning whole genomes and other DNA or protein sequence sets. Its core program, mummer, finds exact maximal matches between a reference FASTA file and one or more query FASTA files. The main entry points, nucmer and promer, build alignments on top of those matches and write a .delta file. A set of show-* tools (show-coords, show-snps, show-aligns, show-tiling, show-diff) and helpers (delta-filter, dnadiff, mummerplot) then parse that output into coordinates, SNP lists, breakpoint classifications, statistics, or plots. Inputs are FASTA; outputs are plain text tables, delta files, and optionally gnuplot or PNG images.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames MUMmer as a system for rapidly aligning entire genomes, noting that version 4 finds all 20 bp maximal exact matches between two bacterial genomes of about 5 Mbp each in 20 seconds using 90 MB of memory. It also positions the tool for draft assemblies, which may contain hundreds or thousands of contigs, and for comparing divergent genomes at the protein level via promer.
brief.how_it_works: mummer uses a suffix-tree based match-finding routine to find maximal matches. nucmer aligns nucleotide sequences all-vs-all and by default keeps only matches unique in the reference, with --mum or --maxmatch to change that. promer translates both inputs in all six reading frames and aligns them the same way, with delta integers measured in amino acids (1 delta int = 3 nucleotides). delta-filter applies a longest-increasing-subset calculation to keep a 1-to-1 or mutually consistent set of alignments.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew is the install path in the entry, but the upstream instructions are source builds. Upstream recommends a release tarball; building from the git tree also needs autoconf, automake, libtool, gettext, and yaggo. Only GCC is supported. On macOS, the README says not to use Clang or Apple's gcc, and to compile with gcc-14 (CC=gcc-14 CXX=g++-14). On FreeBSD, use gmake and gcc14. Ubuntu needs build-essential. SWIG bindings for Python, Ruby, and Perl are optional and need swig, python3-dev, ruby-dev, and libperl-dev. Runtime needs perl5 (5.6.0 or later), sh, sed, and awk on the system path. Optional tools for plotting are gnuplot (4.0+), fig2dev (3.2.3+), and xfig (3.2+). Container builds are documented with Docker and Apptainer.
brief.standout: It is a 2000s-era suite that still ships a suffix-tree matcher, a delta format that a whole family of show-* tools read, and a built-in breakpoint classifier (show-diff) that labels gaps, duplications, relocations, inversions, and translocations. Its promer mode aligns six-frame translations, so proteins can match where DNA has diverged too far for nucmer.
brief.status: unknown. The README has live GitHub Actions build badges for master and develop, and INSTALL.md describes current GCC 14 build steps, which suggests recent upkeep. I saw no release date, last-commit date, or version number in the pages I read, so I cannot confirm the date.
brief.caveats: Only GCC is supported. Clang, including Apple's default toolchain, is not. Building from git needs yaggo and autotools. The README says the docs in docs/ are 'potentially out of date'. Several utilities are obsolete or scheduled for removal: annotate is 'eventually' to be dropped, nucmer2xfig is not properly maintained, and mapview, run-mummer1, run-mummer3, and nucmer2xfig are listed as obsolete in OBSOLETE.md. The README's REPuter note says REPuter is better suited for most repeat matching. The README contact link points to gmarcais/mummer while the repo is mummer4/mummer. I did not see a license statement in the README or INSTALL.md. The Brew caveats field is empty.
